comment: The paste path's bounds (D-CLIP-1, R8), run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js and tests/test_clipboard.py.
A number implemented in two languages gets one fixture (engineering rule, dev branch).
`timeoutMs` is the helper's deadline on the wl-paste read (CLIPBOARD_TIMEOUT, seconds)
and the shell's Model.CLIPBOARD_TIMEOUT_MS; `killGraceMs` is what the helper waits after
SIGTERM before SIGKILL (CLIPBOARD_KILL_GRACE), and the shell's outer watchdog must sit
beyond their sum. `maxChars` is LIMITS.url * 4 in UTF-16 units; `maxBytes` is maxChars
times 4, the most bytes a UTF-8 text of that many units can need. `argv` is what the
helper runs; the shell runs the helper, never wl-paste, since R8.
`replies` are lines the helper could print, and what Model.parseClipboardReply must make
of each: null for anything that is not an ok reply with a string text. Node runs them;
the python test proves the verb prints lines of the accepted shape by running it.

replies.why: an ok reply carries its text
an ok reply keeps control characters for the guide to sanitize
a failure that smuggles a text is still a failure
an ok without a string text answers nothing
an ok with a null text answers nothing
ok must be the boolean true
a blank stdout (a killed helper) answers nothing
a partial line (killed mid-write) answers nothing
a raw text that is not JSON answers nothing
the helper's internal-error payload answers nothing
